Welcome to L.A.M.A.

L.A.M.A. Peruvian Cuisine is a family-owned Peruvian restaurant in Mesquite, Nevada — a taste of Peru in the heart of the Virgin River valley. Our kitchen serves the classics the way they're made back home: bright, lime-cured ceviche, sizzling lomo saltado straight from the wok, golden empanadas, and a cold glass of chicha morada to wash it down.

Come in with the family, settle onto the patio, or order ahead and pick up dinner on the way home. Everything on the menu follows one simple promise — the one written on our door: fresh food made when you order only.

Our Story

Peruvian cooking is one of the great food traditions of the world — a table where Indigenous Andean ingredients meet Spanish, African, Chinese and Japanese influences, and somehow all of it becomes one cuisine. Potatoes and corn from the highlands. Fish from a cold, rich Pacific current. Ají peppers in a hundred colors. At L.A.M.A., that whole story lands on your plate.

Our story in Mesquite starts with a simple idea: this town deserved to taste it. Not a watered-down version — the real thing. Ceviche cured in fresh lime and ají, the way it's eaten in Lima. Saltados fired to order, so the beef, onion and tomato hit the table still sizzling. Causa layered the way grandmothers layer it. Recipes carried from Peru, cooked with pride, and served like family.

Today L.A.M.A. is where Mesquite comes for something different — date nights and family dinners, first-timers curious about ceviche and regulars who drive in for the Peruvian burger and a margarita. Whoever you are, there's a seat for you.

Meet the Owners — Bucci & Lola

Behind L.A.M.A. are Bucci and Lola Bucci. Bucci, the chef, is Peruvian — he grew up on this food, learned it at home and in the kitchens of his homeland, and carried it with him to Nevada. Opening L.A.M.A. was his way of answering a question he couldn't shake: how do I show the people of Mesquite what Peruvian food really is? Every plate that leaves his kitchen is his answer.

Lola is the other half of that answer. Together, the Buccis run L.A.M.A. the way Peruvian families run their tables — generously, proudly, and always ready to pull up one more chair. When you eat here, you're not just a customer walking into a restaurant in Mesquite. You're a guest in their house, tasting Bucci's Peru.
